findings.title: §8 says tests set compressor through createDuel options, but the named opts object only carries helmBars, and a snapshot restore drops helmBars
findings.claim: §5 now defines the option as `opts: { helmBars?: number }` only. §8's lead-in still says the tests 'set HELM_BARS and compressor through createDuel options', so the two texts disagree on where a test's starting compressor comes from. Several tests depend on that start: 'compressor 0 (cap 1000)', 'HELM_BARS 3 with compressor 3', and the new unattended test, which needs thrMille 1000 and so needs compressor 0. Separately, snapshot.ts rebuilds the duel with a five-argument createDuel. A restored duel therefore always gets helmBars 4, which is consistent with 'online uses the default' but isn't stated.
findings.evidence: spec L225-L227 (opts: { helmBars?: number }); spec L342 ('set HELM_BARS and compressor through createDuel options'); spec L345, L350, L375; src/renderer/src/sim/duel/snapshot.ts:L203 (createDuel(layout, seed, 0, playerCount, crewClass)); state.ts:L84
findings.why: A subagent will either add `compressor` to opts (an interface §5 doesn't define) or guess at a field write or helmPower commands. A round-trip test on a helmBars-3 duel would silently restore at 4.
findings.fix: Reword L342: tests set `helmBars` through createDuel's opts and reach a compressor value by writing `d.compressor` after creation, or by sending helmPower. Add to §5 or §7 that a snapshot restore (snapshot.ts L203) uses the default helmBars, like the online authority.

prior.note: §5 L248-L249 now uses max(0, min(3, compressor − lost, HELM_BARS)). Checked: from 4 bars with compressor 1, losing 2 gives compressor 0 and ENGINE 2, so bars come off COMPRESSOR first, then ENGINE. From compressor 3, losing 1 gives compressor 2 and ENGINE stays 1. Merge note (a)-(c) at L250-L257 covers the start split as an owner call, the engine factor reading Engines effective bars, and SIM_VERSION going to whichever spike merges second.

§3 L140-L148 states the unattended newtonianHelm rule: crew.helm = true, the heading turn, helmBoost(d, NO_HELD), crewThrust(thrMille), and rcs 0. It mirrors the existing helmHoldsUnattended branch (step.ts L284-L286). §7 step 2 (L318-L319) references it, and the §8 test is at L375-L376. crew.helm is read only by duel.ts L32 for flight, so setting it unattended has no other side effects. thrust comes after the step-3 ramp, which matches step 7.

§5 L225-L227 names the sixth parameter, its storage as d.helmBars and the pass-through in startRound (step.ts L125). §7 L311-L315 adds DUEL_NOT_SNAPSHOTTED entries for helmBars and helmVent (modules.ts L92 shape), helmPower in commands, unavailable in reasons (modules.ts L63-L64) and the test-list update. A leftover inconsistency at L342 and the snapshot restore are raised as a new P3.

BOOST_FACE_SIN is sin 6°, which is 6×256/360 ≈ 4.27 indices, more than the 4 whole indices a boosted tick can step (2 × 1.778 plus the accumulator). The settle test at L373-L374 now names helmTurn (step.ts L109).

verified: The unattended rule matches today's helmHoldsUnattended branch (step.ts L284-L286), and crew.helm is read only by tactical/duel.ts L32
helmTurn (step.ts L109-L116) orders moveX, then face, then aim, then held heading. With NO_HELD it falls through to headingTurn, so helmBoost(d, NO_HELD) checks the held heading's band
createDuel is positional with five parameters (state.ts L84). startRound (step.ts L125), runtime.ts L251, duelRules.ts L31 and snapshot.ts L203 are its callers
helmModule commands and reasons (modules.ts L63-L64) and DUEL_NOT_SNAPSHOTTED (modules.ts L92-L99) have the shape §7 assumes
Arithmetic for the losing-bars formula and for sin 6° in heading indices
